conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning, Mr. ___ . I'm Dr. ___ , one of your hospitalists. You're here today for your high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy as part of your reinduction treatment for CNS lymphoma. How are you feeling this morning?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Morning, Doctor. I’m doing okay. A little tired, but no major complaints. Just some irritation around my port site, nothing too bad.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Thanks for letting me know. We’ll take a look at your port. Any fevers, chills, nausea, or headaches?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, none of that. I’ve been stable. Just ready to get this cycle done.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s good to hear. We’ll start with some baseline labs and get you set up with IV fluids to help protect your kidneys during the methotrexate infusion. We also need to alkalinize your urine with sodium bicarbonate.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Right, the bicarbonate. I remember that from last time. Is it the same dose?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, same as before—1300 mg every six hours by mouth. It helps prevent methotrexate from crystallizing in your kidneys.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And when will the chemo start?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re scheduling the infusion for around noon today, after we confirm your labs and urine pH is where it needs to be.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, thanks. And my Temodar—do I start that today too?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you’ll start your next cycle of temozolomide today—240 mg daily for seven days, then seven days off. We’ll give you the first dose after the infusion.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my other meds—Levetiracetam, sertraline, the rest—should I keep taking them?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, all your home medications continue as usual—your seizure, depression, and blood pressure meds. We’ll make sure they’re given on schedule.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. And my desmopressin for diabetes insipidus?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll continue that too—10 mcg nasal three times a day. But we’re watching your sodium closely because of the large IV fluids and desmopressin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Right, like last time when my sodium dropped?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. We’re monitoring for that. It’s likely due to the combination of IV fluids and desmopressin causing your body to retain water. But we’ll adjust if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi again. We’ve confirmed your labs and urine pH is optimal. The chemotherapy team is about to start your methotrexate infusion—19,440 mg over several hours.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a big dose. I hope I tolerate it well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: So far, you’re doing great. We’ll monitor you closely. Most patients feel okay during the infusion. We’ll check your methotrexate levels over the next couple of days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your labs are back. Your methotrexate level is 0.25, which is coming down nicely. Your sodium is a bit low—130—down from 136 yesterday.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that a problem? It was 132 last time and they held my desmopressin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: This time it’s mild, and since you’re not symptomatic, we’re keeping your desmopressin on schedule. We expect your sodium to normalize once we stop the IV fluids.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So no changes to my meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No changes. We’ll keep monitoring. Your kidney function and liver tests are stable, which is excellent.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the leucovorin?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You started leucovorin rescue 24 hours after the methotrexate, as planned—45 mg every six hours. It helps protect you from methotrexate side effects.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I remember that helps with the toxicity.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just checking in. Your latest methotrexate level is down to 0.08, which is excellent. That means it’s clearing well from your system.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great news. Does that mean I can go home soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, likely tomorrow. Your sodium is improving, and you’re stable. We’ll stop the IV fluids and bicarbonate, and send you home with instructions to resume your normal routine.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I still need the leucovorin at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, you’ll stop the leucovorin and bicarbonate after today. Your levels are low enough that you don’t need them anymore.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my desmopressin?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, resume your regular desmopressin schedule at home. The low sodium should resolve now that you’re off IV fluids.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. You’re doing well. We’ve reviewed everything, and you’re cleared for discharge today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. Any restrictions?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No major ones. Stay hydrated, take your meds as prescribed, and watch for any fever, confusion, or weakness. But you’ve handled this cycle very well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my follow-up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You have a clinic visit scheduled for your next Rituxan dose, and an MRI coming up next week. Your oncology team will review the results and plan your next steps.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks, Doctor. I appreciate all the care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. We’ll get your discharge papers ready. Take care, and we’ll see you in clinic.
